# Corrections

This page describes the `corrections` slice of the core plugin `claudetto`.
It is for a user who corrects Claude on the same point in more than one session, and for a contributor who edits the slice.

## The Problem

A correction of the user stays only in the context of one session.
After a compaction, a handoff, or a new session, Claude can make the same error again.
A rule in `CLAUDE.md` loads at the start of a session, and in a long session Claude obeys it less (`I02` in [Failure Gaps 0.1.0](Failure-Gaps-0.1.0)).

## What the Hook Does

1. A `prompt.submit` hook runs on each prompt that the user writes, from the composer, a bridge, or the SDK.
   A prompt that a hook or a command adds gets no corrections.
2. The hook reads `.claudetto/corrections.md` in the project.
   When the file does not exist, or cannot be read, the prompt goes on with no change.
3. The hook takes the items of the file and adds one context text to the prompt.
   The text names the file and tells Claude to obey each item in this turn.

The hook makes no model call and matches no words of the prompt.

## Write the File

Write each correction as one item of a Markdown list:

```markdown
- Run `just check` before you say that the work is done.
- Write the commit messages with semantic line breaks.
  Start each sentence on a new line.
```

- An item is a line that starts with a hyphen or an asterisk, and then a space.
- An indented line after an item is a part of that item.
- Each other line, such as a heading or a paragraph, is not in the context.
- Only the last 5 items go into the context, so put the newest item at the end.
- An item is cut at 300 characters.

## Cost

The context text of 5 items of 300 characters is at most about 420 tokens for each prompt.
A file with no item adds no text.

## Bounds

| Bound | Value | File | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CORRECTIONS_MAX` | 5 | `slices/corrections/limits.ts` | Most items in the context |
| `CORRECTION_CHARS_MAX` | 300 | `slices/corrections/limits.ts` | Most characters of one item |

The other bounds of the slice are on [Bounds](Bounds).
